list.name: site
list.label: Site
list.description: Which tzsp-monitor instance these panels read. Remote sites are the REMOTE_SITE_* lines in properties.yml of the instance serving this Grafana; each is a datasource pointed at that site's own InfluxDB, so nothing is copied between sites. Controls never follow this box: rule suppression and reverse DNS only ever act on the local site, and are inert while another site is selected.

list.name: ip
list.label: IP Address
list.description: Pick a host to drill down into (matches either source or destination).
list.query:
import "influxdata/influxdb/schema"
union(tables: [
  schema.tagValues(bucket: "network_traffic", tag: "src_ip"),
  schema.tagValues(bucket: "network_traffic", tag: "dst_ip")
])
  |> group()
  |> distinct(column: "_value")
  |> sort(columns: ["_value"])
  |> keep(columns: ["_value"])

list.name: top_peers
list.label: Top peers (internal)
list.description: Hidden helper: the top-30 peer IPs of $ip, fed to the reverse-DNS resolver.
list.query:
sent = from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.src_ip == "${ip}")
  |> group(columns: ["dst_ip"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> rename(columns: {dst_ip: "peer"})
  |> keep(columns: ["peer", "_value"])

recv = from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.dst_ip == "${ip}")
  |> group(columns: ["src_ip"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> rename(columns: {src_ip: "peer"})
  |> keep(columns: ["peer", "_value"])

union(tables: [sent, recv])
  |> group(columns: ["peer"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_value"], desc: true)
  |> limit(n: 30)
  |> keep(columns: ["peer"])
  |> rename(columns: {peer: "_value"})

panels.title: Top 30 Peers of $ip (Reverse DNS, Country, bytes sent + received)

sent = from(bucket: "network_traffic")

  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.src_ip == "${ip}")
  |> group(columns: ["dst_ip"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> rename(columns: {dst_ip: "peer"})

recv = from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.dst_ip == "${ip}")
  |> group(columns: ["src_ip"])
  |> sum()

from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.src_ip == "${ip}" or r.dst_ip == "${ip}")

  |> sum()
  |> group()

panels.title: Last 10 Flow Records for $ip

targets.query:
from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.src_ip == "${ip}" or r.dst_ip == "${ip}")
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_time"], desc: true)
  |> limit(n: 10)
  |> keep(columns: ["_time", "src_ip", "src_country", "dst_ip", "dst_country", "protocol", "application", "category", "bytes", "packets", "duration_ms"])

panels.description: src_country / dst_country are the GeoIP countries the collector tagged the flow with (blank on flows recorded before it had a GeoIP database).

panels.title: Reverse DNS and Country of $ip
panels.description: Country from a local GeoIP database (IP geolocation by DB-IP, db-ip.com); "private network" for any non-public address.

panels.title: MAC Address and Vendor of $ip (from ARP)
panels.description: Which MAC answered ARP for this address in range, and who made the NIC (IEEE registry; "(randomized)" = a locally administered address the device made up). Recorded by arp-watch, so it exists only for hosts on a segment whose ARP the mirror carries -- an address behind a router never ARPs here, and its frames carry the router's MAC anyway. Two rows mean two MACs claimed it: a new lease, or ARP spoofing -- click a MAC to check on the Ethernet Attacks board.

targets.query:
base = from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "arp_binding" and r.ip == "${ip}")

cols = ["mac", "vendor", "vlan", "_field", "_value"]
packets = base
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "packets")
  |> sum()
  |> toFloat()
  |> keep(columns: cols)
first = base
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "first_seen")
  |> last()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with _value: float(v: r._value) * 1000.0}))
  |> keep(columns: cols)
last = base
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "packets")
  |> last()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with _field: "last_seen", _value: float(v: int(v: r._time)) / 1000000.0}))
  |> keep(columns: cols)

// More than one row here means more than one MAC answered for this address
// in range: a new lease, or somebody impersonating it -- the Ethernet Attacks
// board says which.
union(tables: [packets, first, last])
  |> group()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({r with vendor: if exists r.vendor then r.vendor else ""}))
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["mac", "vendor", "vlan"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> sort(columns: ["last_seen"], desc: true)

defaults.noValue: no ARP seen for this address

value.title: This MAC on the Ethernet Attacks board

panels.title: Traffic of $ip by Peer Country (top 15, bytes)
panels.description: Bytes $ip sent to and received from public peers, by the peer's country. From GeoIP tags the collector writes (IP geolocation by DB-IP, db-ip.com): flows recorded before it had the database are not counted, and private peers are never a country.

targets.query:
// Bytes $ip exchanged with each country: its peers' GeoIP country, from the
// collector's src_country / dst_country tags (tag filter + group + sum, all
// pushed down). Private peers are not a country and are left out, and so are
// flows recorded before the collector had a GeoIP database.
sent = from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.src_ip == "${ip}" and r.dst_country =~ /^[A-Z]{2}$/)
  |> group(columns: ["dst_country"])
  |> sum()
  |> rename(columns: {dst_country: "country"})

recv = from(bucket: "network_traffic")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "network_flow" and r._field == "bytes")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r.dst_ip == "${ip}" and r.src_country =~ /^[A-Z]{2}$/)
  |> group(columns: ["src_country"])
  |> sum()
  |> rename(columns: {src_country: "country"})

union(tables: [sent, recv])
  |> group(columns: ["country"])
  |> sum()
  |> group()
  |> sort(columns: ["_value"], desc: true)
  |> limit(n: 15)
  |> rename(columns: {_value: "bytes"})
  |> keep(columns: ["country", "bytes"])
